description: Replaces College Drive pedestrian overpass with accessible at-grade crossing.
Located between Cumberland Avenue and Campus Drive.

chips.text: Approved (7-3)
7 for, 3 against
Administration recommended Option 3, while Councillor Ford advocated for Option 4.
Decision proactively meets future federal accessibility standards expected by 2027.
The current BRT signal system will not be advanced for real-time adaptive traffic flow.
University of Saskatchewan supports removing the overpass for an accessible at-grade crossing.
Councillor Ford argued the overpass is well-used and the safest option for many pedestrians.
The existing overpass has outstanding accessibility issues that a retrofit cannot address.

description: Grants tax abatements for 85 affordable housing units.
Allocates $3.4 million for 60 supportive housing units.
Includes a warming and cooling community space.
Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation operates 25th Street East.

chips.text: Approved
10 for, 0 against
Councillors questioned city's operating funding commitment for warming/cooling space.
Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation detailed extensive experience addressing homelessness and addictions.
Project targets low-income households and Indigenous people experiencing homelessness.
Ahtahkakoop Cree Nation committed to serving all community members, not just Indigenous.

speakers.name: Lanny Ahenakew
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City Owned Land - Affordable Housing Incentives
said: Nation faces homelessness, addiction challenges in urban centers.
Suited to deliver housing, support services to Indigenous population.
Combines Western and Indigenous best practices for effective outcomes.

speakers.name: Paul Marjerrison
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: City Owned Land - Affordable Housing Incentives
said: Project offers safe warming/cooling space, transition supports.
Provides sober living, long-term support to prevent relapse.
Segregated design ensures safety for all residents and guests.
